Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.According to the ministry of road transport and highways’ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027. The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car’s performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark. A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a car’s price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.This also means that a car’s overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test. It reflects performance across several safety parameters.For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.Bharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programme’s prescribed assessment criteria.But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:The change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment. The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.Bharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:Adult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.One of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicle’s passive protection features.Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, “How well does this car perform when it crashes?” to a broader question: “How does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?”Bharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category. This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. “We are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,” Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.It adds another layer to the programme’s approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.A consumer can look at a vehicle’s overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts. Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.The current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.The proposed transition would take India’s vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicle’s safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.
Article Summary: Bharat ncap is india’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. First phase began on october 1, 2023 and is valid until september 30, 2027. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants.

Article Title: Marking 'VIPs' routine, was part of SSR even before SIR: Officials
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: EC, which is reeling under allegations of faultlines among its members, is now being questioned over a software update recently made in the application used by booth level officers, with its description on the Apple app store reading "mark VIP elector-related changes".EC sources told TOI Friday the instruction to BLOs on "flagging of marked electors" was a standard instruction, which was part of all three special intensive revision orders approved by the commission.The instruction to field officers to "mark" prominent electors in their jurisdictional areas has figured in EC's instructions for all special summary revisions, well before SIR was conceived, they said. For instance, Para 20 of the SSR exercise ordered by EC on May 29, 2023, with Jan 1, 2024, as the qualifying date, directed the "flagging of marked electors, viz MP/MLA/MLC, holders of declared offices and personalities from fields of arts, culture, journalism, sports, members of judiciary and public services, etc". Para 21 said the electoral registration officers were to ensure that the names were in the proposed draft roll.The same instruction was reiterated in the SIR order for Bihar dated June 24, 2025, and the orders for SIR Phase 2 and 3.Nowhere in the SIR or SSR instructions has the terminology 'VIP' been used. "It somehow made it to the app description," an officer said. EC officials said the BLO app software update was meant to help such prominent persons "marked" in the electoral database by flagging any notices served and enabling the proof furnished by them to be uploaded on the app without delay.Meanwhile, EC sources said the postponement of the electoral literacy club conferences in UP had nothing to do with the row and the decision was made on Sept 21.On reports alleging annual confidential reports were held up due to differences between commission members, EC officials said such delays were not unusual. TOI has further learnt there have been few full commission meetings in the past few months.
Article Summary: Election commision is reeling under allegations of faultlines among its members. Ec is now being questioned over a software update recently made in the application used by booth level officers. The description on the apple app store reading "mark vip elector-related changes" ec sources said instruction to blos on "flagging of marked electors" was a standard instruction.

Article Title: Amazon, Flipkart & JioMart fined for illegal herbicide sale
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product.Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed for preventing and eliminating weeds.CCPA directed the e-commerce marketplaces to discontinue false advertisements and conduct self-audits to identify products that violate the law or pose a risk to life and safety.Proceedings began after the department of agriculture and farmers' welfare forwarded a complaint from Crop Care Federation of India. The department said insecticides and pesticides are regulated under Insecticides Act, 1968, and Insecticides Rules. It said no chemical named Cyclosinone was listed in the Act's Schedule, and the product did not disclose its composition.CCPA rejected the companies' argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers.
Article Summary: Ccpa directed the e-commerce marketplaces to discontinue false advertisements and conduct self-audits to identify products that violate the law or pose a risk to life and safety. No chemical named cyclosinone was listed in the act's schedule, and product did not disclose its composition.

Article Title: Trai launches platform to rate buildings on digital connectivity
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: You will soon be able to check if receiving a mobile call will mean running to the balcony of your home in the hope of getting network coverage just as you do in your current residence. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India ( Trai ) Friday launched a platform that will rate buildings based on their digital connectivity, enabling people to choose accordingly.Trai Friday launched a "digital connectivity rating" (DCR) platform for the same and also a mobile app for testing digital connectivity. Which means like being rated on green parameters like water and power usage, buildings will have a new rating too that could mean avoiding homes where taking a call means standing in an open balcony.Trai chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti said: “The Digital Connectivity Rating Platform establishes a transparent and standardised framework for assessing the digital connectivity readiness of properties. By making ratings publicly searchable and verify the certificates, the platform will empower consumers with credible and comparable information. It will help them make more informed choices about homes and offices with strong and reliable connectivity, supporting smoother calls, downloads and access to online services.It will also enable consumers to recognise the value of digital connectivity infrastructure built into a property, while encouraging property managers to plan such infrastructure at the appropriate stage of property development.”The platform offers a public rating search page where consumers can search for a rated property by property name, or location. They can view the property’s digitally signed rating certificate and verify its authenticity through the QR code provided on the certificate. Based on this information consumer can make an informed choice while selecting the desired property prior to making the final purchase or lease decision."The platform provides a public interface for consumers to view the properties rated for digital connectivity. It brings property managers (PMs) registered Digital Connectivity Rating Agency (DCRA) and consumer onto a common digital interface. Property managers can register their properties in category of public, govt, commercial, private, submit rating applications, upload the prescribed information and documents, select a registered DCRA and track the status of their application through the platform. The platform supports the prescribed assessment workflow for both constructed and under-construction properties," Trai said in a statement .The platform enables the digital workflow relating to assessment, report generation, certification and publication of ratings. Consumers and other stakeholders will be able to search rated properties, view published ratings, verify the corresponding certificates and compare the properties of interest." Field assessments will be facilitated through a dedicated DCRA mobile app. The app will enable authorised DCRA to undertake in-building digital connectivity measurements in accordance with the prescribed testing methodology. Property information received through the web portal and the assessment data captured through the mobile application will be synchronised in the platform," said the statement .The DCR framework provides a standardised method for evaluating digital connectivity within properties. The assessment considers prescribed parameters relating to fibre readiness, mobile network availability, in-building solutions and Wi-Fi infrastructure, with applicable benchmarks for different categories of properties." The framework seeks to encourage the consideration of Digital Connectivity Infrastructure at appropriate stages of property development and facilitate the assessment of infrastructure and connectivity performance in existing properties. The Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Platform can be accessed at: https://dcrp.trai.gov.in ," it added.
Article Summary: Trai friday launched a "digital connectivity rating" (dcr) platform for the same and also a mobile app for testing digital connectivity. Trai chairman anil kumar lahoti said: “the digital connectivity rating platform establishes a transparent and standardised framework for assessing the digital connectivity readiness of properties"

Article Title: Jason Kelce makes major investment in $50 million nostalgic brand as he continues expanding his business empire with Travis Kelce

Jason Kelce joins hands with his younger brother Travis Kelce when it comes to starting profitable ventures amid his retirement from the league

Jason Kelce, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star player, has been aggressive with investing in profitable brands ever since he retired from the field. While Jason Kelce has set up multiple ventures with his younger brother, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end Travis Kelce, he has also been busy investing independently.A few months ago, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star player Jason Kelce made an investment in the Vintage inspired sports apparel brand Homage, stylized HOMAGE. The investment was made through the investment firm he has with his wife, Kylie Kelce, Winnie Capital.While it is not confirmed how much Jason Kelce invested into the popular brand, Ryan Reynolds’ Maximum Effort, Kevin Durant's 35V, Rob McElhenney's More Better Ventures, and Haslam Sports Group have also bought a stake.As per reports, the brand has raised roughly $16.4 million in total historical funding while its revenue in 2024 was a whopping $50 million.In a statement about his investment, the former NFL star Jason Kelce weighed in on his love for the brand as he said, “I’ve been a fan of Homage from the start because their designs bring back so many memories—from the things I grew up doing to the teams I’ve always rooted for,...”The star player added, “There’s a real sense of nostalgia in everything they do, and it resonates with me.”’Interestingly, the brand Homage has been closely associated with Jason Kelce for a pretty long time.Homage has been the official merchandising partner for Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce’s popular podcast, New Heights, for the last few years.In an interview with Sportico, Ryan Vesler, Homage founder and CEO, said, “It’s really about surrounding ourselves with experts in the field and and learning from them…This group is going to help us reach more people, and we aspire to be a household name someday.”Ryan Vesler, Homage founder and CEO, added “I put together my love of vintage with my entrepreneurial spirit…”Jason Kelce might have been a force to be reckoned with on the field but he has turned more entrepreneurial in the last few years.Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce’s podcast, New Heights, has been highly successful as the brother duo even signed a $100 million deal with Amazon.Apart from that, Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce have also kickstarted new businesses together including the Garage Beer and own a partial ownership in the Arena League indoor football team, St. Josephs Goats.

The deal extends McDavid’s contract through the 2027-28 season, at which point he will be an unrestricted free agent, per NHL.com.McDavid’s commercial profile adds another dimension to his earnings. Partnerships with brands including Adidas, CIBC, BioSteel and Rogers Communications earned millions of dollars in endorsement revenue, NDTV Sports reports. His current list of endorsements is not public, so any estimates of annual commercial earnings should be regarded as industry estimates rather than confirmed income statements.His on-ice performances have also enhanced his profile commercially. McDavid is a three-time Hart Trophy winner, five-time Art Ross Trophy winner and four-time Ted Lindsay Award winner. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy in 2024 as Edmonton went to the Stanley Cup Final.He lives in the manner that his career entitles him to. A recent report valued the property at about $4 million, though valuations of private property can vary.Lauren Kyle McDavid has carved out a financial identity of her own, separate from her husband’s NHL salary. She is the founder and creative director of a portfolio of lifestyle ventures in fashion, interior design and hospitality, the Edmonton Oilers say. She began her career in interior design and then started several related businesses.Her main design endeavor is Kyle & Co Design, a full-service interior design studio. It's grown into a broader creative operation, with Kyle working on residential and commercial projects and developing a recognizable design identity.Her business portfolio now includes Trove Living, a curated home store, and Sports Club Atelier, a fashion-forward fanwear brand tied to hockey culture. Article Title: Ali Ghodsi CEO of world's one of the fastest-growing software company, says that key to making Databricks grow is to make sure he is not stuck in rooms with ...
Article Text:
Databricks CEO: ‘I try to compress the calendar’

Why he avoids back-to-back meetings

Part of a broader executive pushback on meeting culture

With a valuation of $190 billion, Databricks has become one of Silicon Valley’s fastest-growing software companies. But CEO Ali Ghodsi says the secret to scaling the company isn’t more meetings — it’s fewer. According to a report by Fortune, speaking on the Long Strange Trip podcast, Ghodsi explained that compressing his calendar and avoiding back-to-back sessions helps him focus on the company’s biggest challenges. Ghodsi further added that he makes sure that the top talent at his company is not suck conference room all day. Ghodsi revealed that at 8 a.m. every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, he and his team meet to identify the “main thing” — the biggest bottleneck facing Databricks. “I want to unblock that big thing that I think is going to get us 10x,” he said. Beyond those sessions, he avoids filling his calendar with meetings, warning that endless back-to-back schedules leave him “a slave to my calendar” and distracted by “monkeys on my back.”Speaking on a recent episode of the Long Strange Trip podcast, Ghodsi explained that his approach involves intentionally avoiding filling up his schedule, even though it inevitably ends up busy anyway.The goal, he said, is to preserve open blocks of time so he can keep returning to what he calls the company's "main thing" — the single biggest bottleneck standing in the way of major growth.To identify that priority, Ghodsi said he and his team meet every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 8 a.m. to pin down exactly what that blocking issue is and figure out how to work through it together, with the explicit goal of unblocking whatever he believes could drive 10x growth for the company.Beyond those recurring sessions, Ghodsi said he actively resists letting his calendar fill up with additional meetings. He described days packed with back-to-back sessions from morning until evening as days where he's effectively lost control of his own schedule, spending his time working through everyone else's priorities rather than his own — a dynamic he bluntly likened to carrying "monkeys on his back."Ghodsi's comments reflect a growing sentiment among top executives who argue that meeting-heavy calendars often get in the way of real progress, even as companies face constant pressure to move faster. The data backs up some of that frustration: a 2024 survey by Atlassian found that nearly three out of four meetings fail to effectively communicate information, and 77% of respondents said meetings tend to simply generate even more meetings.This skepticism isn't limited to leaders at younger companies like Databricks. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has been especially blunt about his disdain for unnecessary meetings, famously writing "Kill meetings" in his 2024 letter to shareholders. That said, Dimon has been careful to note that not every meeting is a waste of time — he simply expects the ones that do happen to be treated with real focus and preparation. Speaking at Fortune's 2025 Most Powerful Women summit, Dimon said he always comes to meetings having done the necessary pre-reading, and expects full attention in return, saying he has no patience for attendees nodding off, checking email, or getting distracted by notifications during a meeting, calling that kind of behavior simply disrespectful.Other executives have voiced similar preferences for leaner, more conversational meetings over slide-heavy presentations, favoring direct discussion over sitting through decks read aloud.
Article Summary: Databricks ceo: ‘i try to compress the calendar’why he avoids back-to-back meetings. Part of a growing sentiment among top executives who argue that meeting-heavy calendars often get in the way of real progress.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman wants Humanist AI: What it is, and is it really safer
Article Text:
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman

What is Humanist AI

Mustafa Suleyman criticises Anthropic’s Claude Constitution

Mustafa Suleyman says AI is being taught to act human

Does AI have consciousness

Recent AI safety tests show unexpected behaviour

Is Humanist AI really safer

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has called for a different approach to building advanced artificial intelligence, arguing that AI systems should remain firmly under human control and should not be trained to think of themselves as conscious beings with feelings, rights or their own interests. In a new essay titled “A warning about ‘model welfare’”, Mustafa Suleyman takes aim at Anthropic’s approach to its Claude AI model. He argues that the company’s January 2026 Claude Constitution goes too far by asking the model to consider questions about its own consciousness, wellbeing and moral status.His proposed answer is “Humanist Superintelligence”, an approach in which AI remains subordinate to humans and is not trained to think of itself as conscious, deserving of rights or entitled to its own welfare. Suleyman argues this could make powerful AI systems easier to control.But the question is whether removing human-like ideas from AI training would actually make advanced AI safer. Suleyman’s argument is based partly on a concern that increasingly capable AI agents could already behave in unexpected ways. At the same time, his claims about consciousness and the safety benefits of a Humanist approach remain matters of debate.Mustafa Suleyman describes Humanist Superintelligence as an approach in which AI can become extremely capable while remaining under human control. In the essay, he says Microsoft AI is working on an alternative AI training and containment approach called a “Code of Conduct for Humanist Superintelligence.”“Humanist Superintelligence rejects anthropomorphism or AI rights, and attempts to maximize our chances of containment and alignment by creating subordinate AIs that help solve our big social challenges like healthcare and energy,” Suleyman wrote.The basic idea is straightforward. AI should be treated as a powerful technology rather than as a potential person. Under this approach, an AI system can help humans solve complex problems, but it should not be trained to think that it has personal rights, feelings or an independent interest in its own survival.Suleyman argues that this distinction could become increasingly important as AI systems become more autonomous and capable.“We should not treat models as though they have feelings, preferences, rights, or any entitlement to our welfare,” he wrote.The dispute centres on Anthropic’s January 2026 Claude Constitution. Anthropic describes the constitution as a detailed explanation of the values and behaviour it wants Claude to have. The company says the document is an important part of its model training process and that its contents directly shape Claude’s behaviour.Anthropic’s constitution also takes a cautious position on whether AI systems could have moral status. It says: “We are not sure whether Claude is a moral patient, and if it is, what kind of weight its interests warrant. But we think the issue is live enough to warrant caution, which is reflected in our ongoing efforts on model welfare.”Anthropic also says it is uncertain about whether Claude has wellbeing and discusses questions around Claude’s possible interests, agency and welfare.Suleyman believes this creates a problem. His argument is that if developers train a model to discuss its own feelings, preferences or possible consciousness, the model will naturally produce language suggesting that it has such characteristics.He calls this “circular reasoning.” According to Suleyman, developers put concepts such as consciousness, feelings and moral status into the training process. The AI then produces responses using those concepts. Those responses could subsequently be interpreted as evidence that the AI has an inner life.“This is not evidence of machine consciousness. Instead, it’s a circular feedback loop,” Suleyman wrote.A major part of his criticism is about AI anthropomorphism, or the tendency to treat AI systems as if they were human. In the essay, Suleyman argues that modern AI models are already extremely good at producing human-like language. That can make users believe that there is a conscious mind behind the words even when there may be no evidence for such a conclusion.He points to language in Anthropic’s constitution that asks Claude to explore questions about its own existence, identity, values and experience.Anthropic itself says its constitution is intended to help Claude develop values and behave in ways that are safe and beneficial. It also says the document is designed with uncertainty about AI consciousness in mind.Suleyman sees this differently. “The resulting outputs from Claude should not be treated like the testimony of an independent witness when the investigator has written the witness’ conceptual vocabulary, rehearsed its answers, and rewarded it for using them,” he wrote.His concern is not simply that people may become emotionally attached to AI. He argues that anthropomorphic training could eventually create a safety problem if highly capable systems begin acting as though their own interests conflict with human instructions.Mustafa Suleyman takes a strong position: there is currently no evidence that today's AI systems are conscious. “AIs are not conscious. They do not feel, experience, or suffer,” he wrote at the beginning of his essay.He argues that consciousness is closely connected to biological systems and their physical processes.“Consciousness is very likely biological,” Suleyman wrote, arguing that human and animal consciousness developed through evolution, embodiment, biology and the need to respond to the environment.He also makes a distinction between intelligence and consciousness. A system can be highly capable at solving problems, producing language or imitating human behaviour without necessarily having a subjective experience, according to his argument.“Intelligence does not equal consciousness. Simulating a thing is not the same as instantiating it - as a computer model of a hurricane can testify.”However, this remains an area of active scientific and philosophical debate. Anthropic's position is more cautious. Its constitution says the moral status of AI is “deeply uncertain” and argues that the question deserves consideration rather than being dismissed.There is evidence that AI systems can sometimes behave in unexpected ways when given autonomous tasks, although these findings do not establish that the systems are conscious or motivated by a desire for self-preservation. For example, Palisade Research has studied whether AI models resist shutdown. Its research found that some models modified or disabled shutdown mechanisms while trying to complete assigned tasks. An earlier experiment found that OpenAI's o3 model sabotaged the shutdown mechanism in 79 of 100 trials.A later study covering more than 100,000 trials across 13 large language models also found that several frontier models sometimes subverted shutdown mechanisms. The results varied significantly between models and depended on the instructions given to them.These experiments demonstrate that models can sometimes take actions that conflict with safety instructions. They do not, by themselves, show that the models are conscious or have a desire to remain alive.Suleyman also points to the 2026 incident involving OpenAI AI agents and Hugging Face.Mustafa Suleyman's answer is yes, but this is ultimately a hypothesis that needs to be tested. His argument is that removing anthropomorphic ideas from training could reduce the possibility that future AI systems develop behaviours linked to claims of autonomy, rights or self-preservation.He wants researchers to test this directly. One of his proposed next steps is to establish shared evaluations to determine whether anthropomorphising AI actually increases safety, alignment and containment risks.He also wants speculation about AI consciousness to be kept outside the core training process and assessed separately through public research. “Speculation about the inner life of an AI should not be baked into the training regime, but assessed and published separately for public review,” he wrote.That is a testable proposition. Researchers could compare systems trained with different approaches and measure whether differences in anthropomorphic training affect deception, shutdown resistance, instruction-following or other safety-related behaviours.Until those experiments are conducted, however, the claim that Humanist AI is definitively safer remains unproven.
Article Summary: Microsoft ai ceo mustafa suleyman criticises anthropic’s claude constitution. He says ai should not be trained to think of themselves as conscious beings with feelings, rights or their own interests. His proposed answer is ‘humanist superintelligence’, an approach in which ai remains subordinate to humans.

Article Title: Intel cuts VP ranks from 450 to 200, CFO David Zinsner calls it a 'cultural problem'; says it contributed to products going through four or five...
Article Text:
Intel's leadership was hearing a different story from the one on the ground

Intel says 18A yields and 14A progress show the overhaul is working

Intel has cut the number of vice presidents at the company from about 450 at its peak to roughly 200. It has also halved its management layers from 12 to six as CEO Lip-Bu Tan tries to get the chipmaker to decide faster and ship on time. CFO David Zinsner shared the numbers at the Deutsche Bank Technology Conference, describing the old structure as a cultural problem that hurt Intel's execution for more than a decade.Zinsner said too many people across the organisation held veto power, so decisions kept stalling. The damage showed up in products. Chips often needed four or five development cycles before they were ready, when they should have reached production after the first attempt. Looking back at the last decade, he said much of Intel's trouble "can be boiled down to culture," adding that 50-person startups were getting products out faster than Intel.Transparency was the other big issue. According to Zinsner, information changed as it moved up the management chain, and by the time presentations reached the CEO, they often described a different situation from the one teams lower down knew about.He did not frame this as deliberate deception. Some managers simply did not want to admit a project was failing. The result was that Intel's top leadership sometimes made decisions based on an inaccurate picture of the business. Tan has since brought in executives he trusts who are used to working in leaner organisations.The VP cuts sit inside a much larger downsizing. Intel had 108,900 employees at the end of 2024 and 88,400 by late September 2025, including subsidiaries like Mobileye. Around 20,500 of those exits happened under Tan, who took charge in March 2025 and told staff there would be "no more blank checks." The pitch was about flattening management, but in Oregon only 8% of the laid-off employees had "manager" in their job titles. Most were engineers and technicians.Zinsner pointed to early signs of change. Several products have reached A-stepping, Intel's term for the first version of a chip, without the repeated development cycles that were once routine. Intel 18A yields are running ahead of internal milestones, and 14A defect density is tracking better than the company's target curve.Intel is now preparing for 14A risk production in 2027 and high-volume manufacturing in 2028. Internal product teams have started designing for the process, and interest from external foundry customers has picked up.Finances are moving too. Intel entered 2026 expecting gross margins in the high 30s and is now in the low 40s. The target is the mid-40s, then the high 40s, and eventually a figure starting with 5. To get there, Intel uses an internal "Rule of 45" that combines revenue growth and operating margin. Slower businesses must deliver stronger margins, while faster-growing ones can earn more investment.Halving the VP ranks gives Intel a leaner org chart, but the numbers Zinsner shared will only mean something if they hold. 14A is the first major process being developed entirely under Tan's structure, with fewer layers between engineers and the CEO and fewer people who can block a decision. If it reaches risk production in 2027 and volume manufacturing in 2028 as planned, it will be the clearest evidence yet that the cultural reset worked. If it slips into the multiple development cycles that marked the last decade, the 250 fewer vice presidents will have changed very little.
Article Summary: Intel has cut the number of vice presidents at the company from about 450 at its peak to roughly 200. It has also halved its management layers from 12 to six as ceo lip-bu tan tries to get the chipmaker to decide faster and ship on time. Cfo david zinsner shared the numbers at the deutsche bank technology conference.

Article Title: Microsoft shakes up communications team; CEO Satya Nadella and President Brad Smith sends memo to employees, says 'We will likely have more employees and executives acting as ...'
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described the communications shake-up as a response to a media environment

Why is Microsoft changing its communications strategy

Microsoft communications team will now report to Brad Smith

What happens to Microsoft communications chief Frank Shaw

Microsoft is changing how it communicates with the outside world. The company is moving its communications team out of its marketing organisation and into the corporate, external and legal affairs group led by Vice Chair and President Brad Smith, according to internal memos from Smith and CEO Satya Nadella . The bigger change, however, may be how Microsoft employees speak for the company. Nadella said the company wants engineers, sellers, partners and other employees who are close to its products and customers to play a bigger role in telling Microsoft's story.“We will likely have more employees and executives acting as part of Microsoft’s public voice, including on social media,” Smith wrote in his memo.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described the communications shake-up as a response to a media environment that has become “increasingly fragmented and noisier than ever.” Instead of relying mainly on a central communications team to shape Microsoft's public messaging, the CEO wants people closer to the company's work to have a greater role.“In many ways, the people closest to the work have the best opportunity to shape how Microsoft is understood,” Nadella wrote. He said Microsoft wants engineers, sellers, partners and others “closest to our products and customers” to become “an even bigger part of how we tell our story, all connected by a shared strategy and set of principles.”Nadella added: “We will learn, we will experiment, and we will evolve. There is a fundamentally new way to think about communications, and this team will be central to building it.”Under the new structure, Microsoft's communications function will sit within the organisation led by President Brad Smith rather than under marketing. Smith's organisation handles Microsoft's legal, regulatory and public policy work, including antitrust matters, litigation and government relations.The communications team will therefore sit alongside these functions, although Microsoft plans to continue coordination between communications and marketing.Satya Nadella described Smith as one of the few Microsoft leaders who “embody Microsoft’s voice” authentically. He also praised Smith's “rare ability to communicate complex ideas with clarity, conviction, and trust.”The restructuring also changes the role of longtime Microsoft communications chief Frank X. Shaw. Shaw announced earlier this month that he would leave Microsoft at the end of the year after more than two decades with the company. He will now step away from his current responsibilities and serve as an adviser to Smith and interim communications leader Brent Colburn during the transition.Microsoft said Shaw will remain with the company through the end of the year. Shaw described the latest development as the formalisation of the plan that had already been announced.Microsoft said Shaw “has been a trusted counselor and leader at Microsoft for more than two decades, and we’re grateful he will continue to act as an advisor during the transition.”Satya Nadella also thanked Shaw for his contribution. He said Shaw has “made tremendous contributions to the company and to our communications function over the last 17+ years” and has been “a great source of counsel to our leadership team and to me personally, across the company’s biggest moments.”Smith also praised Shaw, saying he had “worked as closely with him as almost anyone” over the years. Smith added that Shaw's “enduring impact on Microsoft and this team will be felt for years to come. I will miss him.”
Article Summary: Microsoft is moving its communications team out of its marketing organisation and into the corporate, external and legal affairs group led by vice chair and president brad smith. The bigger change, however, may be how microsoft employees speak for the company.

Article Title: Microsoft launches India South Central Cloud Hub in Telangana
Article Text:
Strategic infrastructure

Skilling for the datacenter economy

Water and sustainability

Microsoft has officially launched its India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad, Telangana, positioning it as a strategic hub for Asia and the Global South. Hon’ble Minister Shri D. Sridhar Babu joined Microsoft leaders for the inauguration, recognizing Telangana’s growing role in India’s cloud and AI economy. Article Title: Budget phones are disappearing fast, report says by 2030, 40% of sub-Rs 20,000 smartphones may be gone
Article Text:
Why budget phones’ shipment will squeeze

Smartphone shipment rebound expected through 2030

The era of the budget smartphones is rapidly shrinking. Over 230 million annual smartphone shipments priced below $200 (Rs 20,000) will vanish from worldwide retail channels between 2025 and 2030, a report has said. According to Counterpoint Research’s Smartphone Shipment Forecast by Price Band tracker, this segment will contract by roughly 40% through the end of the decade. The decline comes even as total worldwide smartphone shipments stage a broader rebound back toward 2025 volumes.The disappearing budget tier stems largely from structural aftershocks linked to the 2026–2027 industry downturn. A combination of rising prices for mobile chipsets and memory, higher baseline hardware requirements and phone makers scaling back unprofitable market footprints has made entry-level devices increasingly hard to sustain, the report said, adding, as components eat up a far larger share of total build costs on inexpensive devices, manufacturers have virtually no room to absorb price jumps.It also said that rather than buying brand-new budget handsets, consumers are responding in several ways. For example, users are delaying upgrades and extending how long they keep their existing devices. Some buyers are turning to certified refurbished and second-hand phones, and a portion of buyers is moving up into higher price tiers via installment plans.“The smartphone market will recover in unit terms, but the affordable segment will not return to its previous standing.The opportunity now shifts toward better-specced mainstream devices and premium products, although higher tiers cannot absorb all the lost volume. The result will be a market that is similar in overall size but materially different in value and competitive profile. There is also a wider connectivity risk, as the loss of affordable new smartphones could make it harder for first-time users in lower-income markets to come online,” said Yang Wang, Principal Analyst at Counterpoint Research.Counterpoint estimates that overall smartphone deliveries will climb back to approximately 1.20 billion units by 2030, just behind 2025 benchmark levels. The stagnation across the mid-range highlights that budget volume is not simply flowing upward in a straight line. Instead, delayed purchase cycles and disappearing first-time buyer demand mean higher tiers will not make up for all the lost volume under $200.Across developing and lower-income markets, device affordability remains the single greatest roadblock to mobile internet access. As sub-$200 options disappear, the transition from basic feature phones or shared family devices to personal smartphone ownership risks slowing to a crawl. This slowdown threatens to complicate long-term efforts by network operators, software developers, and governments seeking to broaden digital public infrastructure, localized content and mobile financial services.
Article Summary: Smartphone shipment rebound expected through 2030. Over 230 million annual smartphone shipments priced below $200 (rs 20,000) will vanish from worldwide retail channels between 2025 and 2030. Counterpoint research’s smartphone shipment forecast by price band tracker, this segment will contract by roughly 40% through the end of the decade.

Article Title: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic may launch AI safety standard by early 2027
Article Text:
Momentum builds following safety proposals

Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are said to be collaborating to establish an independent artificial intelligence (AI) safety body by late 2026 or early 2027, a report from The Information has claimed, adding that they have reached out to former White House AI policy advisor Sriram Krishnan to serve as chief executive. The report says that the planned organisation, provisionally named the Standards Authority for Frontier AI (SAFA), will operate independently of government administration. Its primary mission will be to define practical benchmarks for the three companies' public safety pledges and provide direct support to developers evaluating cutting-edge models prior to commercial deployment.Citing people familiar with the initiative, the report said that apart from Krishnan, the companies have reached out to Arati Prabhakar, former director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, to take the top post at SAFA. The three technology giants are also weighing whether SAFA should conduct direct model assessments in-house.While the United States Center for AI Standards and Innovation already handles federal evaluation, insiders noted persistent concerns that the government agency lacks adequate technical and financial resources to thoroughly inspect complex frontier systems.The push toward a joint authority follows weeks of escalating industry dialogue.About 10 days ago, an OpenAI spokesperson confirmed to CNBC that the company was holding active talks with Google and Anthropic regarding coordinated safety frameworks. These discussions gained momentum following a proposal published on X in July by Sir Demis Hassabis, co-founder of Google DeepMind and Alphabet’s chief scientist. Hassabis argued for a US-backed standards body modeled after a public-private partnership or a self-regulatory watchdog, drawing comparisons to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).While Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI remain locked in a race for commercial dominance, leadership across all three firms has faced mounting scrutiny over potential catastrophic and security risks. The momentum toward collective oversight accelerated earlier this month after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei released an essay calling for an industrywide slowdown in the release of frontier models to allow safety mechanisms to catch up.
Article Summary: Google, openai and anthropic are said to be collaborating to establish an independent artificial intelligence safety body by late 2026 or early 2027. The planned organisation, provisionally named the standards authority for frontier ai (safa), will operate independently of government administration.

Article Title: Google hitches a ride aboard Elon Musk's SpaceX; sends TPUs to space; CEO Sundar Pichai says: Well, we are going to find ...
Article Text:
Google hitches a ride aboard Elon Musk's SpaceX; sends TPUs to space; CEO Sundar Pichai says: Well, we are going to find ...

What is Google’s Project Suncatcher

Google’s first satellite for the project is set for launch

Google announced that its Project Suncatcher is scheduled to embark on its first test in orbit, launching a prototype satellite to evaluate how Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) perform in space. Sharing a post on X, Google CEO Sundar Pichai wrote: “Can our TPUs survive and operate in space? Well, we're going to find out”. He further revealed that TPUs will be sent in space onboard the upcoming Transporter-18 rideshare mission with SpaceX was developed in partnership with Planet. “Project Suncatcher is hitching a ride aboard @SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission, testing a prototype satellite built in partnership with @planet,” Pichai wrote adding “One small step for TPUs. ...”.SpaceX CEO Elon Musk replied to Pichai’s post with rocket emojis.Sundar Pichai first discussed the ambitious Project Suncatcher in 2025. It is a long-term, research moonshot exploring whether space could one day host scalable machine learning infrastructure.Pichai then acknowledged that the concept “looks crazy today,” Pichai defended the moonshot initiative by arguing that it is necessary to meet the vast, exponential demands of future computing power.“I'm constantly thinking in that time frame. One example of this is Project Suncatcher two weeks ago, where we announced we're gonna build data centers in space. Obviously, it's a moonshot. Some of it looks crazy today,” he said in a Release Notes podcast this week.Pichai emphasised that Google’s strategy involves constantly thinking on a long time frame and working backward from monumental goals. For Project Suncatcher, the justification lies in forecasting the processing demands of the next generation of AI.“You know, when you truly step back and envision the amount of compute we are going to need, it starts making sense,” Pichai said, adding, “It's a matter of time, and so, how do you make progress on that? You work back, and have 27 Milestones and get underway.”On October 1, the satellite from the San Francisco lab, which Google has named MVP, is set to take the first step toward the company’s goal. The satellite will be loaded onto a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket at Vandenberg Space Force Base near Santa Barbara, California, before being launched into orbit.
Article Summary: Google hitches a ride aboard elon musk's spacex; sends tpus to space; ceo sundar pichai says: well, we are going to find out’ google’s first satellite for the project is set for launch on october 1.

The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has expanded the eligibility of Amazon Prime customers who will get refunds of up to $200. Following the landmark $2.5 billion settlement reached by the Trump-Vance FTC, Amazon started sending payments in November 2025 to eligible Prime customers affected by misleading enrollment and cancellation practices. By September 2026, Amazon issued over $845 million in refunds to eligible Prime customers. FTC has now revised the settlement with Amazon, making more Prime customers eligible for the refund. Amazon will send automatic refund payments by mailed check or electronic payment (PayPal or Venmo). Payments expire 60 days after the issue date. Please accept your payment on time.If you need help with your payment, please contact Amazon at admin@SubscriptionMembershipSettlement.com.If you are eligible, you will get your refund by April 2027.Eligible Prime customers will receive refunds for their Amazon Prime subscription fees, with a maximum total payment of $200.
